Dermatology · published research

Hair growth (excluding androgenetic alopecia)

One small post-COVID hair-loss series combined LED treatment with microneedling and growth factors, so the light effect cannot be separated. Most mapped publications are preclinical and some use androgenetic-alopecia models.

PBM Database summary

What the records report

One small post-COVID hair-loss series combined LED treatment with microneedling and growth factors, so the light effect cannot be separated. Most mapped publications are preclinical and some use androgenetic-alopecia models.

Summary of the Evidence

No exact database label captures non-androgenetic-alopecia regrowth. A narrow mapping includes 21 “Hair growth” and one “Hair loss (not AGA)” publication, excluding the dedicated AGA category. The 22 records include one editorial, one small human combination study, nine animal-inclusive and 12 in-vitro publications; three also include ex-vivo work. Method counts overlap, and some laboratory papers explicitly study AGA.

Human and clinical evidence

The only mapped clinical report is an open-label series of ten people with post-COVID hair loss. It combined LED with microneedling and growth factors. Average density rose from about 47 to 58 hairs per cm² at 20 weeks, but the difference was not conventionally significant. Participants were classified using AGA staging, and some had mixed shedding and pattern loss. The cohort does not represent one defined non-AGA cause, and the light effect cannot be separated from co-treatments (Gentile et al. 2022).

Animal evidence

Eight mouse and one rat studies report changes in hair-cycle timing, follicle-cell migration, or regrowth. Models and protocols differ, and some are androgen-sensitive or AGA-related. A mouse injured-skin study reported follicular responses after red light but does not establish efficacy for a human alopecia (Zhang et al. 2021).

In-vitro and ex-vivo evidence

Twelve in-vitro and three ex-vivo publications include cultured dermal papilla cells and isolated follicles. Findings concern protocol-dependent proliferation, migration, hair-cycle markers, and signaling. Several papers are AGA-focused; a 650-nm red-light study used follicles from people with AGA, not other hair-loss causes (Yang et al. 2021).

Treatment Parameters and Generalizability

The clinical combination used 423-nm blue visible and 640-nm red LEDs with microneedling and growth factors, without isolating light dose. Model studies vary in wavelength and schedule. No common therapeutic window or head-to-head protocol is established for non-AGA conditions.

Interpretation

Experimental follicle work is broader than the direct human evidence, which is one small, confounded series with mixed diagnoses. AGA models remain indirect. The set does not establish that PBM alone restores hair in a defined non-AGA condition.

Evidence strength in source summaryVery low for clinical hair regrowth outside androgenetic alopecia
Publications and records22 articles (narrow mapped set)

Evidence strength rationale and next steps

The only mapped human report enrolled ten people with post-COVID hair loss but combined LED treatment with microneedling and growth factors; the measured density change did not meet conventional statistical significance. Most other publications are animal or laboratory work, often involving androgenetic-alopecia models. A controlled study in a defined non-AGA condition that isolates light from co-treatments would support a stronger rating.
